Subject: Post-demo recap — payment path & procurement prep for POC

Hi Emily — great to meet today, thanks for the time and the thoughtful questions. Quick recap and suggested next steps from our side: 

- Recap: We covered the 30-day POC scope (50 seats, basic integration, latency targets). You indicated success criteria and timeline (pilot start late Oct, evaluation 30 days).
- Question we need to lock down: preferred payment route for the pilot (PO / invoice / procurement card / AWS Marketplace). You mentioned internal constraints on POs for small pilots — can you confirm the threshold?
- Info we can share now: sample invoice, standard purchase terms, and a short SOW for signature. Attached: BrightWave_PO_Specs.pdf (PO fields you mentioned) and a quick copy of our purchase terms.

Ask: Can you confirm by EOD whether procurement will: 1) allow a procurement card payment, 2) require prepay, or 3) insist on a PO-only flow for vendors without marketplace listings? Knowing this will determine whether we file a payment-exception request on our side.

If procurement wants to avoid card/pay-in-advance, we can propose a one-time prepay invoice for the pilot or discuss a marketplace route — we have an AWS marketplace listing in-progress but it won't be live until November.

Next steps: 
1) Emily — reply with procurement preference and any PO-form fields (vendors contacts).
2) If PO not allowed, Laura will loop Sales Ops to propose an exception or prepay invoice.
3) If card ok, Marissa will provide payment link and quick onboarding invoice.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

Best,
Laura Bennett

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — payment path & procurement prep for POC

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. A few notes from Procurement side: 

- Policy baseline: For pilots/sub-$50k engagements we typically route payment via procurement card (P-Card) or credit card. Our standard Net-30 PO process applies only for approved vendors with a vendor profile and a marketplace footprint.
- Marketplace restriction: We cannot issue a standard PO for new vendors that are not in AWS Marketplace unless Finance signs off on vendor onboarding (security onboarding + W9 on file). That process can take 10–14 business days.
- Prepay: Our policy generally does not allow vendor-initiated prepayments for vendors under our master vendor policy unless there is a legal exception. We would need a written business justification and Procurement approval.

For this pilot specifically: Finance asked whether Redwood can accept payment via procurement card or provide an invoice we can pre-approve but pay via P-Card. If you require prepay (vendor collects before delivery), we will need a formal exception.

I can do the P-Card for <$25k without additional approvals; above that threshold I'll need Procurement head approval. Please advise:
1) Can Redwood invoice and accept payment via procurement card?
2) If card is not supported, can you issue a prepay invoice or do you require a PO first?

Thanks — I can escalate internally once I have the exact asks from your side.

Emily Carter
Senior Procurement Manager | BrightWave Health
emily.carter@brightwavehealth.com

Subject: RE: Post-demo recap — payment path & procurement prep for POC

Laura / team — thanks for the heads-up. A few options and recommended language to move this forward quickly: 

- Option A (fastest): Accept P-Card for pilot up to $25k. Marissa to provide a payment link and an interim invoice. Require customer confirmation email acknowledging pilot terms.
- Option B (if P-Card not allowed): One-time prepay invoice for the pilot amount. Finance can issue a standard pro-forma invoice; customer pays via ACH or card. Redwood will apply payment to the pilot and issue a final invoice once the pilot converts. 
- Option C (when PO required): If BrightWave requires a PO-only workflow, we need their vendor onboarding checklist completed (W9, insurance certificate if requested) — that will add ~2 weeks.

Given Emily's note about the $25k auto-approval threshold, recommend proposing Option A for speed. If BrightWave needs prepay, we'll request a short exception from Finance to accept vendor prepayment (we will provide a custom pro-forma and a SOW). 

Action items for Sales (Laura): Reply to Emily with the proposed Option A and include the payment link template. If they push for prepay/PO, loop me and I'll prepare the prepay invoice and exception wording to send to your procurement contact.

Also tagging Karthik to confirm that pilot SOW language we plan to use is acceptable for prepay/invoice handling.

Marissa Cole
Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

1) Can Redwood provide a short DocuSign SOW + a customer-facing invoice template (so we can attach it to the P-Card transaction)? A draft SOW link would be very helpful.

3) If Redwood prefers marketplace billing (AWS MarketplacE), please indicate ETA for listing — Finance would favor that path but understands it isn't available for this week.

If you can provide the DocuSign SOW + invoice template today, I'll initiate the P-Card payment this afternoon. Otherwise, I can start the procurement approval request if pilot budget will be >$25k.

Best,
Emily
